I have farmed this land in Ntchisi for many years, and I know maize will not grow well without fertilizer, so I will use both the chemical fertilizer from the government program and manure from my animals. My grandchildren will help with planting and weeding, but I will hire some young men for the heavy digging because at 86 my bones are too weak for that work now. We depend only on the rains here, so I cannot irrigate, and I do not buy those expensive sprays—I pull weeds by hand just as my father taught me. I always plant the improved seed because it gives a better harvest than the old local varieties.
